runs.summary: Data through Nov 23 (Q4 38-day partial). Top 3: XLE +36.6%, CIBR +33.2%, SMH +27.8%. SPY P/E: 22.34x
runs.content:
Top 5 YTD 2026: XLE +36.6% (P/E 12.99x, Cheap), CIBR +33.2% (31.70x, Elevated), SMH +27.8% (23.68x, Fair), XBI +20.8% (20.48x*, Fair, profitable holdings only), XLP +18.6% (25.01x, Elevated).

Bottom 5 YTD 2026: XME -17.7% (14.03x, Cheap), GLD -16.0% (P/E N/A), GDX -15.1% (11.53x, Cheap), ICLN -13.2% (17.27x, Fair), XLC -11.2% (14.78x, Cheap).

Notable shifts: sharp sell-off, then a violent rebound. SPY fell 8.6% in the week to Nov 20 and rose 4.7% on Nov 23 (Q4 -5.3%, YTD +6.7%). SMH fell 17.8% in that week, then rose 15.0% on Nov 23; XLE missed the rebound (-1.1%). No sector rose over the six sessions since Nov 13; CIBR (-0.2%) held up best. Three band crossings, all downward: XME and XLC Fair -> Cheap, SMH Elevated -> Fair; no sector is Expensive. Momentum: XRT, XLF, XLY Breakout -> Fading; KIE Breakout -> Consolidating; XLV Accelerating -> Continuing; ITA Fading -> Reversing. XLP (Q4 +12.1%) is the only Breakout left. 13 of 25 sectors beat SPY YTD; 7 are negative YTD (was 5). The run was a day late and mid-session, so returns were cut off at the Nov 23 close. JETS failed in the batch download and was retried successfully. SPY, SMH and JETS closes match a second source.
